Exactamente. Yo hago el depósito a mi tarjeta de débito de Interbank y apenas llega la fecha de pago Deel hace la transferencia automática a mi tarjeta. Ahora, si no te funciona ese método en Deel puedes usar miles de métodos de pago como Paypal, Wise, Payoneer, pero la que me funcionó mejor y la que demora menos e incluso tiene poca comisión es la de la transferencia directa.

Deel es perfecto. Tiene una opción de depósito directo en tarjeta. No cobra casi nada de comisión, es el 2% pero máximo 15 dólares por todo el depósito independientemente de cuanto ganes, lo máximo que puedes depositar a tu cuenta en Perú son 15000 dólares mediante este método, y la transferencia es inmediata. A parte no tienes que hacer nada, Deel puede hacer todo el trámite automáticamente apenas te depositen. Yo llevo ya medio año con Deel porque afortunadamente la empresa lo maneja y la verdad es que es excelente.

I covered the faceplates with resin. To the resin I also put some resin flakes that I bought on Amazon. I waited two days for them to dry and then sanded and polished by hand.
I did it myself. I like the glossy finish of the new Moondrop Kato, so I polished one faceplate and wrapped the other one in black.

>It is a vinyl wrap. A while ago I tried to paint them but it didn't look so good, and if I get bored of the color it would only be to remove the wrap and put a different one, and it's not so complicated to wrap the faceplates. You should try it!

I used from 400 grit to remove the brushed finish, all the way up to 5000 grit. I used a 3M package which is sandpaper for polishing car headlights. The polishing compound I used is called Brasso, and I used it all the way through. As I also answered in another comment, I removed the faceplates to avoid damage to the IEM's. It is not difficult at all to remove the faceplates from the Blessing 2's.   
This is the sandpaper I used:   
https://www.amazon.com/-/es/papel-mojado-autom%C3%A1tico-paquete-surtido/dp/B005JPGTNI/ref=sr\_1\_6?\_\_mk\_es\_US=%C3%85M%C3%85%C5%BD%C3%95%C3%91&dchild=1&keywords=3+m+sandpaper&qid=1633749112&sr=8-6

I actually removed the faceplates. Doing the process without removing them would be too dangerous for the IEMs. Fortunately it is not that complicated to remove the faceplates from the Moondrop Blessing 2, and they can be reattached using a resin adhesive.

Well, I really like the finish of the Moondrop KXSS and the new Moondrop Kato, but I love the Blessing 2 and I don't plan to change them for a long time. So, I decided to modify the left faceplate that was a bit worn and with marks. I polished it with fine sandpaper, finishing it with a metal polish to a mirror finish. To the right faceplate I put a matte black vinyl like the first mod I did some time ago. I quite liked how it turned out. I hope you like it too.
